claim.natural: Every red-blue edge-colouring of K_20 contains two pairwise vertex-disjoint monochromatic copies of K_4, while some red-blue edge-colouring of K_19 contains no such pair; the two copies need not have the same colour.

limitations: The upper bound reuses the parent z(20) candidate's two fixed-core reduction, Ramsey-core catalogue, exact CNFs, and proof objects rather than independently reproducing them.
Certificate checking establishes unsatisfiability only for the two exact CNFs.
The catalogue generator, nauty canonicalisation, and graph-to-CNF source implementation are not formally verified, and the graph-to-CNF equivalence remains a separate written proof obligation.
The upstream result is itself an unrefereed candidate with no reported complete human verification, independent external reproduction, or end-to-end formalisation.
dependencies.statement: The inherited lemma that every graph on 20 vertices has two vertex-disjoint homogeneous four-sets is exactly the K_20 upper-bound obligation after identifying red edges with graph edges and blue edges with nonedges. The unrelated z(20) residual cocolourability computations are not dependencies.

downstream.statement: The result may be cited or investigated only as the immutable unrefereed candidate determination that VR_2(K_4)=20, with copies permitted to differ in colour. It must not be represented as peer reviewed, independently reproduced, completely human-verified, or formally proved end to end. Its lower construction is hand-checkable, while its upper bound reuses the pinned fixed-core dependency; the checked certificates establish only the two exact CNFs, with the catalogue and graph-to-CNF bridge remaining separate obligations. No uniqueness or enumeration of 19-vertex extremal colourings is claimed, and the offline snapshot does not constitute a complete objection search.
